newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria unions plan general strike for Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria unions plan general strike for Wednesday.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest trade union organisation has called a nationwide one-day strike for Wednesday to demand a cabinet reshuffle and early parliamentary elections, union officials said.

Miners and teachers are expected to be among the most militant groups supporting the strike. Union officials from Sofia city transport said they would work normally, and airport staff said they had not yet decided whether to join the strike.
By law, health workers, telecommunications staff, the army and the police are forbidden to strike.

"We shall protest against the incompetence and corruption of Zhan Videnov's Socialist cabinet which has led the country to levels of poverty and misery unseen in the past," said Confederation of Independent Trade Unions (CITU) spokeswoman Snezhana Lyubenova.
"The strike is expected to be a stepping stone towards early parliamentary elections which will prevent Zhan Videnov cementing his cabinet's position through the introduction of a currency board."
Workers at the Uranovo mine in Blagoevgrad will stop work for an hour on Tuesday evening, a CITU statement said.
It said rallies would be held in the towns of Plovdiv, Bourgas, Stara Zagora and Dobrich.
Severe economic crisis has increased pressure on the governing Socialists, whose candidate suffered a decisive defeat in presidential elections last month.

The anti-communist opposition has called for early elections and says it will not support a currency board regime proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise the economy if it is implemented by the present government.
The currency board, a form of fixed exchange rate regime likely to be introduced early next year, will strengthen Videnov's position if he is seen as bringing back stability.

Wednesday's strike, in which for the first time in seven years the union is raising political demands, takes place less than three weeks before a Socialist Party congress expected to discuss calls for policy reform and cabinet changes.
